Who pays: borrowers (10% of interest goes to the protocol), flash borrowers (0.09%) and liquidated accounts (10% of the liquidation bonus). Earnings so far are test amounts: $0.06.

Not done: no confirmed outside users yet, no audit, and one owner key on testnet. A trove costs 1% a year and pMUSD pays 0.06% today, so minting to supply only pays above about 39% utilisation. Timelock and multisig moved to December. veMEZO and gauges were left out of this wave.

All four Wave 2 goals are done and live on Mezo testnet. Every lease is new real-world demand for MUSD: rent is borrowed against BTC each month and paid to landlords in MUSD.

App: https://mezo.rentouts.co

1. Pay monthly (done). The tenant funds the deposit plus the first month, then pays each month. If a month stays unpaid a full period past its due date, the landlord can claimDefault: the funded rent plus at most one month from the deposit; the rest returns to the tenant. Up front for a $2,000 x 12 lease drops from 26,000 MUSD to 4,000. withdrawAndPayRent mints each month's rent from the tenant's own trove only when it is due, so no prepaid MUSD sits idle. This is our answer to the Wave 1 "idle MUSD" feedback: the Stability Pool pays no MUSD yield and can lose deposits, so we kept deposits out of it (docs/STABILITY-POOL-CHECK.md). Live run: lease #7, 7 transactions from request to deposit back.

2. Borrow and pay in one transaction (done). RentEscrowV2 calls Mezo's BorrowerOperationsSignatures itself: borrowAndFund opens a trove and funds the lease, withdrawAndFund draws on an existing trove, and surplus MUSD comes back in the same transaction. A fresh wallet with only faucet BTC opened its trove and funded lease #4 in one tx: https://explorer.test.mezo.org/tx/0xc3a379e0a40e2934ad61bccb1c6eed89c084310fb79a0cb2243bce12c1d20d8e

3. Mutual early termination (done). proposeTermination / acceptTermination on exact, hash-bound terms; the escrow splits the balance with no arbiter. Lease #2: landlord 15 MUSD (rent + agreed penalty), tenant 35 back.

4. Dispute timeout (done). resolveByTimeout: if the arbiter doesn't rule in time, earned rent goes to the landlord and the rest to the tenant (30 days in production, 600 s on testnet). Lease #3 settled this way.

5. New: redemption safety. The "Your trove" tab now shows where you stand in Mezo's redemption queue (and how much MUSD is ahead of you), and lets you claim any BTC left over if a redemption closes your trove.

6. Also added: a Your trove panel (repay, add or withdraw BTC, close, live ratio and liquidation price; Recovery Mode blocks new borrowing), a revenue model (escrow stays fee-less; 1% landlord fee off-chain in the rentouts.co portals) and worked user scenarios.

New since our wave 1 submission (commit 79c3e67, Oct 21, 2026).

What we learned. We surveyed Malagasy developers paid from abroad (FaceDev Facebook group, Oct 28-30, 10 responses, 9 of them paid from abroad). Honest reading: their payments mostly work. 8 of 9 say the last one went fine, 5 of 9 used a bank transfer, 8 of 9 lost under 3% or nothing they know of. What remains is trust: one waited days to be sure the money had arrived; one met a client who said "I paid" while nothing arrived, a fake proof of payment and a dispute on the amount; one lost a bitcoin payment to a reseller when converting to ariary. 4 of 9 have received or held crypto. A small, tech-savvy sample from one group: not representative.

What we built, live on Mezo testnet:
1. "Was I really paid?" on the merchant's ledger. Paste what the client sent: a message, a screenshot's text, a transaction hash, a PayLink invoice or receipt link. Code extracts the hashes, links, amounts and tokens (MUSD, dollars, BTC, sats); the answer comes only from Mezo testnet: the transaction receipt and its Paid event from our PayLinkV2 contract (0x448eCce9711860502806A3d5B021a4f9Ba715082), or the contract's state for the merchant's invoice. Paid shows the exact amount, the token, the block, the time and the invoice it paid, to the merchant's own address. Not received says why: a made-up hash, a payment to someone else, an unpaid or cancelled invoice, a failed transaction, an old receipt sent again for a new invoice, a forged receipt link. Pending and "Can't tell yet" say so instead of guessing. The message never leaves the device; no AI and no server decides.
2. "Paste the client's message" on the create page: fills the MUSD amount and the link's validity from the client's message, by fixed rules in English, French and Malagasy, labelled "no AI". Our AI drafting assistant, built for another edition, runs on a server that does not accept the Mezo app yet; we will not change it while that edition is judged.

w2_update:
Wave 2 answers every point from the Wave 1 review, and delivers our declared Wave 2 goals: the idle MUSD reserve now earns and compounds into the loan, and one owner can run many vaults. The on-chain rules registry moves to Wave 3.

1. The MUSD reserve now earns. Idle reserve goes into the Mezo Stability Pool (provideToSP) and earns BTC from liquidations. When the loan is in danger, protect() pulls just the missing MUSD back out (withdrawFromSP) and repays. harvest() adds the BTC gains to the trove as collateral, so the loan protects itself with its own yield. The agent keeps 30% liquid and pools the rest by itself. Mezo blocks pool withdrawals while any trove is under 110%; protect() catches that and falls back to the liquid reserve and BTC buffer instead of reverting.

2. Redemption surplus (the High finding). claimSurplus() calls BorrowerOperations.claimCollateral() and sends the BTC to the owner. The agent calls it automatically after a redemption.

3. Min debt cap. maxRepay() = debt - 200 MUSD gas compensation - minNetDebt. protect() clamps to it on-chain and the rules engine never asks for more, so a rescue cannot revert at Mezo's 1800 MUSD floor.

4. Revenue model. 0.5% of each rescue and 10% of Stability Pool gains, to a treasury fixed at deploy. Hard caps in the contract (1% and 20%). A failing fee transfer never blocks a rescue.

5. A pitch deck and a launch video. Explorer verification: we rebuilt for the london EVM and the deployed bytecode matches our build byte for byte, but Mezo's verifier still answers Unable to verify, so the contracts are not verified yet.

Also: agent writes carry a gas margin because Mezo's trove list search costs 6M+ gas on testnet (found when a live rescue ran out of gas), closeLoan() unwinds the pool to pay the debt, the agent serializes its transactions (fixed a nonce race), a new Earn card in the dashboard, the chat explains Earn and fees. w2_update:
In Wave 1, the judge pointed out real problems with the shared master Trove. There was no handling for redemptions or liquidations, users could get stuck if Mezo closed the Trove, and repayments were lowering the master ICR without reducing debt.

We fixed all of that in Wave 2.

Pro-rata write-down
If Mezo takes collateral from the master Trove through redemption or liquidation, every user’s BTC claim is reduced fairly and proportionally. And no user can receive more than they originally deposited.

Smart debt reduction
When a user repays, their MUSD are used to pay down the master Trove debt (as long as the cash buffer hasn't gone below its threshold). We keep a safe floor at 1,810 MUSD so we never break Mezo’s minimum.

Wind-down and exit path
If Mezo fully closes the master Trove, anyone can call enterWindDown(). Users can then call claimInWindDown() to take any remaining BTC and have their debt forgiven. No one gets stuck.

Internal liquidations
Any position below 130% ICR can be liquidated. The collateral stays in the master Trove and strengthens the system for everyone else.

Recovery Mode
New borrows are blocked when Mezo is in Recovery Mode. Repayments also respect the required collateral ratios before any BTC is withdrawn.

Keeper and monitoring bot
We built an autonomous bot that:
- Liquidates underwater users
- Triggers wind-down if the master Trove is closed
- Watches Master ICR, system TCR, and cash buffer
- Sends real-time alerts on Discord or Telegram

### Updates in this Wave

RelayGuard has advanced from a Mezo payment prototype into a more complete merchant payment and operations workflow. The current Wave 2 build supports two MUSD commerce paths: merchants can create exact-value invoices with shareable checkout links and QR codes for customers, and API developers can protect their own Node.js routes with an x402 integration. In both paths, the merchant keeps its own website or API and receives MUSD directly. Invoice status changes to paid only after RelayGuard verifies the matching on-chain token, payer, recipient, and amount.

The checkout experience has been strengthened with wallet-ownership verification, buyer MUSD and BTC/gas preflight checks, protected checkout sessions, and a retry path for canceled wallet confirmations. It also offers eligible buyers an optional, separate Mezo Testnet borrowing flow when they lack enough MUSD. Borrowing requires an explicit quote review, liquidation-risk acknowledgement, and separate wallet confirmation; it does not pay the invoice automatically. This Wave also fixes the case where a wallet with less BTC than the selected collateral could fail during gas estimation: RelayGuard now checks collateral funding first and reports the shortfall. Automated tests cover the borrow quote, transaction submission, receipt confirmation, refreshed MUSD balance, and separation from invoice payment.

On the merchant and operator side, the Wave adds merchant wallet verification, merchant-scoped x402 resources and credentials, explicit operator roles, and controls around treasury actions. Mezo trove health and price data are read at a consistent block; RelayGuard requires human review below its 150% review buffer, blocks below Mezo’s 110% minimum, and pauses MUSD authorization if protocol reads fail. Policy decisions retain trove evidence, and stale approvals cannot proceed after relevant conditions change.

The reviewer experience and submission materials have also been expanded: a public walkthrough separates live contract and receipt checks from controlled policy scenarios; the pitch, technical brief, demo script, and submission deck describe the current product and business hypothesis. name: Levada
tagline: Levada brings Mezo's MUSD Savings Rate to Base.
w2_update:
Levada lets anyone holding MUSD on Base earn Mezo's MUSD Savings Rate without leaving Base. You deposit MUSD on Base and get lsMUSD, a savings token that grows. Levada 
  carries the MUSD to Mezo over Wormhole NTT, the bridge MUSD itself uses, deposits it in sMUSD, and brings the yield back into your balance on Base. Nothing to claim on 
  Mezo, and no BTC needed for gas.

  What we built this Wave:

  Contracts (Solidity, Foundry). LevadaVault on Base is an ERC-4626 vault. It books principal on Base, keeps a 10% buffer for instant exits, and queues larger exits first in,
  first out. LevadaHub on Mezo holds the MUSD in sMUSD, compounds the yield and reports it back over Wormhole. Each report's gain is released into the share price over 12
  hours, so nobody can deposit just before a report and take the yield. The hub fills withdrawals in parts, within what it holds and the bridge's rate limit, so every exit
  completes. Both contracts are immutable and every step is permissionless. The owner can pause and cap new deposits but cannot move funds or block withdrawals.

  Security. An independent adversarial review found 2 high, 1 medium and 8 low issues. All are fixed, each with a regression test. The suite has 38 tests, including fuzz
  tests and invariants (2,000 runs of 100 random actions check that every queued exit completes and nobody loses principal), plus fork tests against the live MUSD bridge and
  sMUSD on Base, Base Sepolia, Mezo and Mezo testnet. The trust model and every fix are in SECURITY.md.

  Keeper. A TypeScript keeper relays Wormhole-signed messages between Base and Mezo, bridges MUSD above the buffer, posts yield reports and pays out queued exits. Anyone can
  run it, and it only pays gas. A GitHub Actions workflow runs it every 5 minutes.

  Web app (Next.js). Save and withdraw with live exit tracking, a live view of where every MUSD is (on Mezo, crossing the bridge, or on Base), a live Mezo market strip from
  DefiLlama, a test MUSD faucet for judges, and a status page.

  Status: code, tests and deploy scripts are complete. Deploying to Mezo testnet and Base Sepolia is the next step.

TL;DR: Mezo apps post quests in MUSD ("open a MUSD loan", "save 50 MUSD in Mezo savings", or their own rule). A user joins, does the action on Mezo, and claims; the contract reads their wallet and pays them. No screenshots, no reviewers.

How it works
- Post: createQuest pulls reward x places in MUSD and deposits all of it into Mezo's MUSD Savings Rate vault (sMUSD), so idle escrow earns.
- Join: refused if the wallet already passes the check, so apps only pay for new usage.
- Claim: at least one block after joining, Muster re-checks on-chain (an active trove in TroveManager, an sMUSD or token balance, or the app's own completed(address) contract), withdraws the reward from sMUSD and pays it.
- Close: after the deadline the poster takes back unpaid places. Nobody can cancel early.
- Revenue: savings yield on idle escrow goes to the treasury. Posters pay no fee.
- No owner, no upgrade, no pause. External checks are gas-capped and wrapped so one bad check can't break other quests.
